heading: Cold open
narration: Silicon accounts for more than ninety percent of semiconductor production by volume, according to SEMI International Standards.

heading: Cold open
narration: That figure tells you the industry's choice, not the physical requirement. A semiconductor is not defined by being silicon.

heading: Cold open
narration: It is defined by having an electrical conductivity you can control through temperature, light, or deliberate contamination.

heading: Cold open
narration: The material itself sits between conductor and insulator, and that middle ground is where the engineering happens.

heading: Title card
narration: What is a semiconductor made of?

heading: Pure silicon conducts poorly until you break its symmetry
narration: Pure silicon at room temperature is a poor conductor. Every silicon atom bonds to four neighbors in a diamond cubic lattice.

heading: Pure silicon conducts poorly until you break its symmetry
narration: Those bonds lock electrons in place. Intrinsic silicon — the term for material with no intentional impurities — has a conductivity millions of times lower than copper.

heading: Pure silicon conducts poorly until you break its symmetry
narration: The crystal is symmetric. Charge carriers exist only when thermal energy breaks a bond, creating an electron and a hole in matched pairs.

heading: Pure silicon conducts poorly until you break its symmetry
narration: That symmetry is the starting point, not the goal. The engineering begins when you break it.

heading: Doping introduces the asymmetry devices require
narration: You make silicon useful by adding impurities at parts-per-million concentrations. This is called doping.

args.title: CONTROLLED DOPING
steps: introduce group-III or group-V atoms at ppm levels
diffuse or implant dopants into crystal
args.note: carrier type and density now engineered

heading: Doping introduces the asymmetry devices require
narration: If you introduce phosphorus or arsenic — elements from group fifteen of the periodic table — each atom brings five valence electrons into a lattice that expects four.

heading: Doping introduces the asymmetry devices require
narration: The extra electron becomes a mobile negative charge carrier. The material is now n-type.

args.title: CONTROLLED DOPING
steps: introduce group-III or group-V atoms at ppm levels
diffuse or implant dopants into crystal
args.note: carrier type and density now engineered

heading: Doping introduces the asymmetry devices require
narration: If you introduce boron or gallium from group thirteen, each atom accepts an electron to complete its bonds, leaving a mobile positive hole.

heading: Doping introduces the asymmetry devices require
narration: The material is p-type. The conductivity is no longer symmetric. You have engineered an imbalance, and that imbalance is what transistors and diodes exploit.

args.title: CONTROLLED DOPING
steps: introduce group-III or group-V atoms at ppm levels
diffuse or implant dopants into crystal
args.note: carrier type and density now engineered

heading: Doping introduces the asymmetry devices require
narration: The ratio matters. One dopant atom per million silicon atoms changes resistivity by orders of magnitude.

heading: The purity requirement is extreme and measurable
narration: Semiconductor-grade silicon begins with purity near one part per billion for electrically active impurities, according to SEMI standards.

heading: The purity requirement is extreme and measurable
narration: That level is measured by resistivity mapping and secondary ion mass spectrometry.

heading: The purity requirement is extreme and measurable
narration: The Czochralski process grows single crystals from molten silicon in a quartz crucible under inert atmosphere.

heading: The purity requirement is extreme and measurable
narration: Oxygen from the crucible dissolves into the melt at parts-per-million levels. Carbon, metals, and dopants from previous runs are removed by zone refining or controlled segregation during solidification.

heading: The purity requirement is extreme and measurable
narration: The purity target is not arbitrary. A single unintended atom per billion can shift carrier concentration enough to ruin a transistor's threshold voltage.

heading: The purity requirement is extreme and measurable
narration: The measurement techniques have detection limits in the parts-per-trillion range for some elements, but production monitoring operates at parts-per-billion sensitivity because that is where electrical properties become reproducible.

heading: Compound semiconductors use two or more elements in fixed ratios
narration: Silicon is an elemental semiconductor. Gallium arsenide, gallium nitride, indium phosphide, and silicon carbide are compound semiconductors — crystals built from two elements in stoichiometric ratios.

heading: Compound semiconductors use two or more elements in fixed ratios
narration: Gallium arsenide has a bandgap near one point four electronvolts compared to silicon's one point one, according to NIST data.

heading: Compound semiconductors use two or more elements in fixed ratios
narration: Gallium nitride reaches three point four electronvolts. Silicon carbide sits near three point three.

heading: Compound semiconductors use two or more elements in fixed ratios
narration: A wider bandgap allows operation at higher voltages and temperatures. Gallium nitride transistors survive junction temperatures above two hundred degrees Celsius.

heading: Compound semiconductors use two or more elements in fixed ratios
narration: Silicon carbide is used in power electronics for electric vehicles because it switches faster and wastes less energy as heat than silicon at equivalent ratings.

heading: Compound semiconductors use two or more elements in fixed ratios
narration: The bandgap is not adjustable after growth. You choose the compound for the application.

heading: The bandgap determines which photons the material absorbs
narration: The bandgap is the energy difference between the valence band, where electrons are bound, and the conduction band, where they move freely.

args.title: PHOTON ABSORPTION
stages: photon energy exceeds bandgap
electron promoted to conduction band
hole left in valence band

heading: The bandgap determines which photons the material absorbs
narration: A photon with energy greater than the bandgap can promote an electron across that gap.

heading: The bandgap determines which photons the material absorbs
narration: Silicon's one point one electronvolt bandgap corresponds to infrared light near one thousand nanometers wavelength.

args.title: PHOTON ABSORPTION
stages: photon energy exceeds bandgap
electron promoted to conduction band
hole left in valence band

heading: The bandgap determines which photons the material absorbs
narration: Gallium arsenide absorbs visible red. Gallium nitride absorbs blue and ultraviolet. This is why blue LEDs require gallium nitride or indium gallium nitride — silicon's bandgap is too narrow to emit blue photons efficiently.

heading: The bandgap determines which photons the material absorbs
narration: The material's composition sets the bandgap, and the bandgap sets the optical response.

args.title: PHOTON ABSORPTION
stages: photon energy exceeds bandgap
electron promoted to conduction band
hole left in valence band

heading: The bandgap determines which photons the material absorbs
narration: You cannot tune a silicon photodetector to see blue light. The physics forbids it.

heading: Crystal structure and defect density matter as much as composition
narration: A semiconductor is not just a chemical formula. It is a crystal with long-range order.

heading: Crystal structure and defect density matter as much as composition
narration: Dislocations — line defects where the lattice is misaligned — trap charge carriers and create leakage paths.

heading: Crystal structure and defect density matter as much as composition
narration: High-performance devices require dislocation densities below ten thousand per square centimeter, measured by etch-pit counting or X-ray topography.

heading: Crystal structure and defect density matter as much as composition
narration: Grain boundaries between misoriented crystals are worse. Polycrystalline silicon is used in solar cells where cost matters more than efficiency, but microprocessors demand single-crystal wafers with controlled orientation.

heading: Crystal structure and defect density matter as much as composition
narration: The crystal is grown, sliced, polished, and mapped for defects before any doping or patterning begins. A chemically perfect composition in a defective crystal is electrically useless.

heading: Producer POV
narration: 'What is it made of' sounds like it wants one element. Silicon is over ninety percent of production, but the defining property is the impurity deliberately added to it, not the base material. I answered the question underneath the question.

heading: Alloys let you tune properties continuously between endpoints
narration: You are not limited to binary compounds. Indium gallium arsenide is a ternary alloy.

heading: Alloys let you tune properties continuously between endpoints
narration: The composition is written as indium-x gallium-one-minus-x arsenide, where x ranges from zero to one.

heading: Alloys let you tune properties continuously between endpoints
narration: At x equals zero you have gallium arsenide. At x equals one you have indium arsenide.

heading: Alloys let you tune properties continuously between endpoints
narration: At intermediate values the bandgap varies smoothly between zero point four and one point four electronvolts.

heading: Alloys let you tune properties continuously between endpoints
narration: This lets you design a photodetector for a specific infrared wavelength by adjusting the indium fraction during growth.

heading: Alloys let you tune properties continuously between endpoints
narration: Aluminum gallium nitride works the same way for ultraviolet. The lattice constant also changes with composition, which matters when you grow one alloy on top of another.

heading: Alloys let you tune properties continuously between endpoints
narration: Lattice mismatch creates strain and defects unless the layers are thin or the mismatch is small. You are trading one parameter against another.

heading: Interfaces between materials create the active device structures
narration: A transistor is not a bulk material. It is a stack of layers with engineered interfaces.

heading: Interfaces between materials create the active device structures
narration: A silicon MOSFET has a p-type or n-type channel, a silicon dioxide gate insulator, and heavily doped source and drain regions.

heading: Interfaces between materials create the active device structures
narration: The oxide is grown by thermal oxidation at nine hundred to eleven hundred degrees Celsius in oxygen or steam.

heading: Interfaces between materials create the active device structures
narration: The thickness is controlled to nanometers by time and temperature. The interface between silicon and silicon dioxide has trap states — energy levels in the bandgap caused by dangling bonds and impurities — that are reduced by hydrogen annealing.

heading: Interfaces between materials create the active device structures
narration: The carrier mobility in the channel depends on interface roughness and charge.

heading: Interfaces between materials create the active device structures
narration: You are engineering boundaries, not bulk. The device physics happens where one material meets another.

heading: Thermal budgets constrain which processes can follow which
narration: Every high-temperature step risks redistributing dopants you placed earlier. Phosphorus and boron diffuse through silicon at rates that double every ten degrees Celsius near one thousand degrees.

heading: Thermal budgets constrain which processes can follow which
narration: If you implant boron to form a shallow junction and then oxidize at eleven hundred degrees, the boron profile spreads.

heading: Thermal budgets constrain which processes can follow which
narration: Process sequences are ordered by decreasing temperature to minimize this redistribution. The highest-temperature steps — oxidation, annealing, epitaxial growth — come first.

heading: Thermal budgets constrain which processes can follow which
narration: Lower-temperature metallization and passivation come last. The thermal budget is the cumulative time at temperature the wafer experiences.

heading: Thermal budgets constrain which processes can follow which
narration: Exceeding it blurs the doping profiles you designed. The composition you engineer is not static. It evolves with every subsequent process step.

heading: Gettering removes mobile contaminants before they reach active regions
narration: Metal impurities — iron, copper, nickel — diffuse through silicon at device processing temperatures.

heading: Gettering removes mobile contaminants before they reach active regions
narration: Even parts-per-trillion concentrations degrade transistor performance by creating mid-gap states that increase leakage current.

heading: Gettering removes mobile contaminants before they reach active regions
narration: Gettering is the deliberate introduction of defects or impurity sinks far from the active device region, usually at the wafer backside.

heading: Gettering removes mobile contaminants before they reach active regions
narration: Phosphorus-doped backside layers or mechanical damage create sites where mobile metals preferentially segregate.

heading: Gettering removes mobile contaminants before they reach active regions
narration: During high-temperature anneals, contaminants diffuse toward these gettering sites and are trapped there.

heading: Gettering removes mobile contaminants before they reach active regions
narration: The technique does not remove impurities from the wafer. It moves them to a location where they do not matter.

heading: Gettering removes mobile contaminants before they reach active regions
narration: The composition of the active region is protected by engineering the composition of the sacrificial region.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: The numbers in this script trace to measurement standards, not marketing. SEMI International Standards publish semiconductor material specifications including purity and resistivity.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: NIST provides bandgap and lattice constant data for elemental and compound semiconductors.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: ASM International documents crystal growth and defect characterization methods. When you see a figure for dislocation density or dopant concentration, it reflects a measurement technique with known precision and known limits.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: The composition of a semiconductor is not a single answer. It is a controlled recipe with tolerances in the parts-per-million range, verified by multiple independent methods.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: The purity figures in this script represent production targets, not thermodynamic limits.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: Published ranges for background oxygen in Czochralski silicon span an order of magnitude depending on growth conditions.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: The exact impurity profile in a finished device is proprietary and varies by manufacturer.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: What is certain is the requirement: electrical properties must be reproducible lot to lot, and that requires composition control far tighter than any other bulk material industry. The measurement exists. The universal profile does not.

heading: Closing
narration: A semiconductor is made of elements chosen for their bandgap, doped with impurities at parts-per-million levels to control carrier type, grown as a single crystal to minimize defects, and stacked in layers to form interfaces where the device physics happens.

heading: Closing
narration: The material is not the silicon. It is the controlled asymmetry inside it.
